newsitem.title: PERU: Lima stocks end off, pare losses on Fed inaction - Sept 24.
newsitem.headline: Lima stocks end off, pare losses on Fed inaction - Sept 24.

text.p: The Lima Stock Exchange closed slightly lower Tuesday, cutting some of its losses in the last 15 minutes of trade on the U.S. Federal Reserve's decision to leave rates unchanged.

The market had retrenched for most of the session on caution ahead of the Fed's announcement. Traders predicted stability or some gains on Wednesday due to an expected entry of foreign investors to the local market.
"The bolsa recovered right at the end, closing on buys," said Aurelio Diaz of Prisma brokerage. "This helped the volume of trade, although the indexes were negative."
In Tuesday's session, the General Index lost 0.91 percent to 1,554.38 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index fell 0.4 percent to 2,079.39.
Total market volume was a low 23.87 million soles ($9.5 million) on 2,353 trades as overall 21 stocks rose, 46 fell and 32 were flat.
"We were waiting to see how New York moved, and according to that, we moved, which produced a cautious day with very low volume," said Manuel Torres of Finvest brokerage.

Benchmark Telefonica del Peru accounted for the largest share of trade, 12.51 percent of the total, and closed stable at 5.59 soles, while brewery Backus y Johnston, with 10.14 percent of the total volume, fell 0.36 percent to 2.75 soles.

Among other leaders, Buenaventura, with 7.11 percent of total volume, was also unchanged at 22.50 soles, while fellow miner Milpo lost 3.02 percent to 3.02 soles, and brewery Cervesur dropped 2.56 percent to 1.52 percent.
